name: HAM10000: Human Against Machine 10000 Dermatoscopic Skin Lesion Benchmark
description: The HAM10000 ('Human Against Machine with 10000 training images') dataset is a multi-source collection of dermatoscopic images of common pigmented skin lesions, curated by the Medical University of Vienna and the University of Queensland and published in Nature Scientific Data. Deposited on Harvard Dataverse, the dataset consists of 10,015 dermatoscopic images accompanied by extensive clinical metadata (patient age, sex, lesion anatomical site, and diagnostic confirmation method: histopathology, confocal microscopy, or follow-up). The benchmark classifies lesions into seven diagnostic categories: actinic keratoses and intraepithelial carcinoma (akiec), basal cell carcinoma (bcc), benign keratosis-like lesions (bkl), dermatofibroma (df), melanoma (mel), melanocytic nevi (nv), and vascular lesions (vasc).

license.notes: The Harvard Dataverse API endpoint (https://dataverse.harvard.edu/api/datasets/:persistentId/?persistentId=doi:10.7910/DVN/DBW86T) reports 'license: null' with Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International terms embedded in dataset-level 'termsOfUse'. All 7 files have 'termsOfAccess: null' and 'restricted: false'. Because the deposit bundles multi-source images and ISIC 2018 challenge test partitions without independent file-level license declarations, the exact license claim is designated as provisional.
